scope: Non-party organisations that helped electors left off the roll or sent notices during the SIR (and Assam's Special Revision). Every quote was checked against the fetched page on 2026-10-09.

organisations.name: Sabar Institute
organisations.what: Ran a helpline and legal aid camps for electors removed from the roll, with legal interns drafting and filing appeals to the Appellate Tribunals online and offline. Published a step-by-step manual on filing appeals.
organisations.source_outlet: Maktoob Media (piece written by a Sabar Institute research associate)
organisations.quote: As part of the Sabar Institute’s initiative, we have set up a helpline and legal aid camps for deleted voters.
organisations.notes: The source is written by the organisation itself, published in Maktoob. Its own site carries an SIR data repository and tribunal lists but no description of the helpline, and no helpline number was found published. The site already links to Sabar Institute from method pages.
organisations.why_not: The site names no compiler of the lists it counts, and its method pages already link to this institute.

organisations.name: United Medicos
organisations.what: Ran a helpline and legal aid camps that helped electors deleted after adjudication file appeals to the Appellate Tribunals.
organisations.quote: In response, Sabar Institute and United Medicos have mobilised a dedicated team on the ground.
organisations.notes: Only one source, written by the partner organisation.

organisations.name: Jamiat Ulema-e-Hind (West Bengal unit)
organisations.what: Ran about 200 camps across 22 districts during enumeration, with a WhatsApp helpline, district control rooms and advocates to help with documents.
organisations.quote: Jamiat has also come up with a WhatsApp coordination group, district-level control rooms, and a team of dedicated advocates across 22 districts to help with documentation.
organisations.notes: DOUBTFUL ON THE PARTY RULE: both reports say the unit was led by a serving state minister of the ruling party in West Bengal. The organisation itself is not a party and said the drive was non-political. No helpline number was published in either source.
organisations.why_not: Led by a serving minister of the ruling party in the state.

organisations.name: All Bengal Minority Youth Federation
organisations.what: Held around 500 camps a day in Muslim-majority areas during enumeration to explain the forms and documents.
organisations.quote: The All Bengal Minority Youth Federation, one of the largest organisations in the community, has also swung into action.
organisations.notes: Second source (Dynamite News) carries the same 500-camps figure. The camps were mainly awareness and form-filling guidance.

organisations.name: Nakhoda Masjid (Kolkata)
organisations.what: Held daily training sessions and help desks at the mosque to guide people through the enumeration form.
organisations.quote: The Nakhoda Masjid and several other major mosques have begun holding daily training sessions outside prayer halls and conducting help desks to guide people through the SIR process
organisations.notes: A religious institution rather than an NGO. Quote is a verbatim fragment; the full sentence ends with an attribution to a named cleric.

organisations.name: Varta Trust
organisations.what: Put together a team of lawyers and peer counsellors to support queer and trans electors facing exclusion during the revision.
organisations.quote: When the SIR was first announced, they anticipated increased distress and put together a team of lawyers and peer counsellors.
organisations.notes: The organisation told the reporter that few people had reached out. Its website was not checked, so how_to_reach is blank.

organisations.name: Dinajpur Notun Alo
organisations.what: A community organisation of trans people in Uttar Dinajpur that supported members through the revision, including those placed under adjudication or removed.
organisations.quote: Over the months, we have been focused on the SIR and supporting our community, but recently with the passing of the Trans Act, I have not been able to follow up on SIR.
organisations.notes: WEAK: the source shows support to its own community, not a public help service, and says the work had slowed.

organisations.name: Amra Padatik
organisations.what: An NGO of sex workers that worked with women in Kolkata red-light areas at SIR assistance camps held with booth-level officers.
organisations.quote: NGO representatives said a total of more than 300 women turned up across three camps in Chetla, Kidderpore and Kalighat during the day.
organisations.notes: The report does not say clearly who organised the camps; BLOs were present. Amra Padatik is named as an NGO present at the Chetla camp.
organisations.why_not: The second reading found no help shown delivered in the source.

organisations.name: Society for Human Development and Social Action
organisations.what: Worked with sex workers in Kolkata at SIR assistance camps alongside two other NGOs, and pressed the Commission to accept cooperative-society documents.
organisations.quote: NGO representatives said a total of more than 300 women turned up across three camps in Chetla, Kidderpore and Kalighat during the day.
organisations.notes: Same PTI report as Amra Padatik. The sentence naming the organisation also names its representative, so the camp sentence is quoted instead.

organisations.name: Bihar State Legal Services Authority (with District Legal Services Authorities)
organisations.what: On the Supreme Court's request, asked District Legal Services Authorities to provide paralegal volunteers and free legal aid counsel to help excluded electors file statutory appeals, and to publish volunteers' contact details village by village. Earlier the Court asked for paralegal volunteers to help with online claims and objections.
organisations.quote: requested the Bihar State Legal Services Authority to issue necessary communication to the District Legal Services Authorities for ensuring the availability of paralegal volunteers and legal aid counsels who can assist the excluded persons in filing appeals.
organisations.notes: DOUBTFUL ON OUTCOME: the sources show a court request, not the help as delivered. At the 16 October 2025 hearing the Commission told the Court no appeals against deletions had been filed. No report of the Authority's status report was found. A statutory body, not an NGO.
organisations.why_not: A statutory body, covered under free legal help.

organisations.name: Citizens for Justice and Peace (CJP)
organisations.what: Ran SIR training and awareness sessions in Mumbai with community groups, covering documents, the 2002 roll linkage, notices, hearings and appeals.
organisations.quote: It is from this history of engagement that CJP, together with Vote for Democracy (VFD), began conducting a series of detailed SIR awareness and training sessions in Maharashtra.
organisations.notes: Training and awareness rather than case-by-case help. CJP is not shown as a party to the SIR cases in the Supreme Court in anything read here.

organisations.name: Vote for Democracy (VFD)
organisations.what: Ran SIR training sessions in Maharashtra jointly with CJP and co-published a training manual on enumeration, notices, hearings and appeals.
organisations.quote: It is from this history of engagement that CJP, together with Vote for Democracy (VFD), began conducting a series of detailed SIR awareness and training sessions in Maharashtra.
organisations.notes: VFD also publishes reports alleging a stolen mandate in Bihar; it is an advocacy platform as well as a help provider.

organisations.name: Jamiat Ulama-e-Maharashtra
organisations.what: Launched an SIR awareness campaign and resolved that local units set up assistance camps and invite booth-level officers to them to help people fill enumeration forms.
organisations.quote: “Do not sit at home waiting for the Booth Level Officer (BLO). Instead, set up local assistance camps, gather the public, and invite the BLOs to these camps to streamline the form-filling process.”
organisations.notes: WEAK: a call to set up camps at a general body meeting, not evidence that camps ran. Salaam People is a small community news site.
organisations.why_not: A resolution to set up camps, with no help shown delivered.

organisations.name: Citizens for Justice and Peace (CJP), Assam team
organisations.what: During the Special Revision, used community volunteers and local meetings to help electors facing objections, took a memorandum and a list of affected electors to the Election Commission, and intervened when ration dealers demanded documents.
organisations.source_outlet: CJP and Vote for Democracy training manual (own publication), p. 35
organisations.quote: Through our awareness meetings, unofficial connections, discussions with the BLOs in our network, and the dedication of our community volunteers, we were able to directly and indirectly assist hundreds of thousa nds of people.
organisations.notes: Assam ran a Special Revision, not an SIR. The quote is verbatim from the PDF text layer, including its broken word "thousa nds". The figure is the organisation's own claim. The same section names a party office-bearer; that is not carried here.

organisations.name: Citizens for Justice and Peace (CJP)
organisations.what: Published a guide explaining SIR notices and what an elector should do on receiving one, and a training manual (with Vote for Democracy) on notices, hearings, documents and appeals.
organisations.quote: Understanding why an SIR notice signals process—not punishment—and what it means on the ground
organisations.notes: The guide body is a PDF embed; the quoted line is the page standfirst.

organisations.name: People's Union for Civil Liberties (PUCL), Rajasthan
organisations.what: Held form-filling camps with booth-level officers in Jaipur during enumeration and set up a response team for SIR problems across Rajasthan.
organisations.quote: Our performance was good, we helped fill and collected more than 300 to 400 forms in the camps that were organised.
organisations.case_name: People's Union for Civil Liberties v. Election Commission of India (writ petition against the Bihar SIR order of 24 June 2025, heard with Association for Democratic Reforms v. Election Commission of India)
organisations.notes: LITIGANT: PUCL petitioned the Supreme Court against the SIR (LiveLaw, July 2025) and says on this page it will continue litigating. The Rajasthan section is written by PUCL office-bearers.

organisations.name: SIR Sachetan Matadhikar Bachao Manch (SSMBM)
organisations.what: A forum formed at PUCL Chhattisgarh's call to deal with SIR problems. It trained volunteers, ran awareness meetings and took specific problems to the Chief Electoral Officer, who ordered forms filled wrongly by one BLO to be redone.
organisations.quote: Apart from meetings to train volunteers and spread awareness, the Forum also met with the CEO-Chhattisgarh to outline the problems people are facing.
organisations.notes: Described by the organisation that convened it (PUCL), so close to an own account. PUCL is an SIR litigant; the forum itself is not shown as one.

organisations.name: Sauhard Evam Bandhuta Manch, Bahadurganj (Ghazipur)
organisations.what: Placed its members at polling stations in Bahadurganj Nagar Panchayat to help the public and BLOs, and set up help desks where people were helped to fill their forms.
organisations.source_outlet: CJP and Vote for Democracy training manual, p. 52
organisations.quote: Furthermore, by setting up help desks at various locations, people were assisted in filling out their forms
organisations.notes: DOUBTFUL ON STATE: the passage sits under a chapter headed Bihar, but names Bahadurganj, Ghazipur, which is in Uttar Pradesh, and a final list after 6 March, which fits the UP timetable. The same sentence says forms were filled through ward councillors and public representatives, so local elected people were involved.
organisations.why_not: The second reading found no help shown delivered in the source.

organisations.name: My Vote, My Right Karnataka (MVMR-K)
organisations.what: A coalition that trained volunteers to run an SIR helpline and help desks in Bengaluru, mainly for migrants, slum dwellers, trans people, Muslims, Dalits and Adivasis, helping with the 2002 mapping and forms. It also took complaints to the Chief Electoral Officer.
organisations.source_outlet: BehanBox (first-person account by a helpline volunteer)
organisations.quote: Seeing how the process played out elsewhere, the MVMR-K coalition prepared by training volunteers like myself to run a helpline and help desks, particularly for communities at greater risk of being disenfranchised—migrants, slum dwellers, trans people, Muslims, Dalits, and Adivasis.
organisations.notes: DOUBTFUL ON THE PARTY RULE: the campaign was launched in October 2025 at a meeting of civil society organisations, political parties, trade unions, women's and student groups (Maktoob, 2025-10-11, https://maktoobmedia.com/india/civil-society-groups-in-karnataka-launch-campaign-against-election-commissions-special-intensive-revision/). Its help desks are described as volunteer-run. No helpline number was found published. A domestic workers' union, Stree Jagruti Samiti, asked for one help desk in its area.

organisations.name: Solidarity Youth Movement (SYM), Haveri unit
organisations.what: Helped people in Haveri district trace their 2002 roll details for the enumeration form, through a WhatsApp group, and held workshops on what to do if a name is missing from the draft roll.
organisations.quote: the SYM had directly helped around 6,000 people in Haveri district, besides conducting awareness workshops on what to do if someone’s name is not on the draft rolls.
organisations.notes: The figure is the organisation's own claim. The quote is a verbatim fragment; the full sentence names a unit office-bearer.

organisations.name: Citizens' vote vigilance committee (Karnataka)
organisations.what: Ran training workshops for volunteers during enumeration and set out to resolve people's doubts, help them complete registration and monitor official help desks.
organisations.quote: Additionally, the committee has decided to resolve people’s doubts and help them complete registration.
organisations.notes: DOUBTFUL ON NAME: Deccan Herald writes it in lower case; SabrangIndia (2026-10-01) reports a Citizens' Vote Protection Committee that worked with an Anti-SIR Alliance which includes secular political parties. They may be the same body; not confirmed. The source states a plan, not help delivered.
organisations.why_not: A plan described, with no help shown delivered, and possibly linked to an alliance including parties.

organisations.name: Voter Adhikar Manch (VAM)
organisations.what: A citizens' collective of groups working with workers and migrants that ran helplines and physical help desks in working-class localities across Delhi, helping electors with progeny mapping and forms and taking their cases to the Chief Electoral Officer.
organisations.quote: We have assisted numerous people with progeny mapping, and the struggle to figure out the exact details of the polling booth in the exact assembly constituency that has been redrawn extensively in Delhi, where their parents would have voted 24 years ago, is harrowing.
organisations.notes: Also The Wire, 2026-07-28: "The Voter Adhikar Manch also set up help desks which have received around 50 calls per day with complaints." It has said it may go to court; no case was found. No helpline number was found published.

organisations.name: Catholic Archdiocese of Hyderabad
organisations.what: Among the church bodies that set up help desks across Hyderabad, staffed by trained volunteers, to help voters complete enumeration forms.
organisations.quote: The Catholic Archdiocese of Hyderabad, All India Peoples Mission and the Telangana Council of Churches were among those organising the help desks.
organisations.notes: One report only.

organisations.name: All India Peoples Mission
organisations.what: Among the church bodies that organised help desks in Hyderabad to help voters complete enumeration forms.
organisations.quote: The Catholic Archdiocese of Hyderabad, All India Peoples Mission and the Telangana Council of Churches were among those organising the help desks.
organisations.notes: One report only.

organisations.name: Telangana Council of Churches
organisations.what: Among the church bodies that organised help desks in Hyderabad to help voters complete enumeration forms.
organisations.quote: The Catholic Archdiocese of Hyderabad, All India Peoples Mission and the Telangana Council of Churches were among those organising the help desks.
organisations.notes: One report only.

organisations.name: Youth Welfare Telangana
organisations.what: Prepared about 60 advocates, most of them in the districts, to volunteer for electors receiving verification notices after the draft roll.
organisations.quote: They are trained to volunteer in the next crucial period of the SIR exercise,
organisations.notes: WEAK: shows preparation before notices went out, not help delivered. The quote is a verbatim fragment of a statement attributed to the founder.
organisations.why_not: Preparation only, with no help shown delivered.

organisations.name: Sabar Institute
organisations.what: Its legal experts co-conducted training for those preparing to help Hyderabad electors at the notice stage, drawing on the West Bengal experience.
organisations.quote: Legal experts from the Kolkata-based SABAR Institute are co-conducting training and sharing data insights and operational strategies based on their experience in West Bengal.
organisations.notes: DOUBTFUL ON THE PARTY RULE: the sentence follows one on AIMIM deploying 250 advocates, and the report does not say whose training Sabar co-conducted. It may have been the party's. Check before listing.

excluded_parties.name: All India Trinamool Congress, "May I Help You" SIR camps (West Bengal)
CPI(M) West Bengal, legal teams for deleted voters
AIMIM, SIR awareness drive and voter assistance campaign (Hyderabad)
DMK, SIR helpline for cadres (Tamil Nadu)
BJP Lucknow, campaign to add missing names with Form 6
Congress, ward-wise drive to restore names (Vasco, Goa)
CPI(ML) Liberation and RJD, assistance with Form 6 (Bihar, per the Commission in the Supreme Court)

not_found: Bihar: no civil society or NGO help service was found with a source; only the court-directed Legal Services Authority route.

Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Goa, Puducherry, Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Jharkhand, Haryana, Punjab, Uttarakhand and the North-East: no non-party organisation found with a checkable source. Reports name government help desks (Kerala village offices, Chennai Corporation centres) and party desks only. PUCL reports unnamed civil society camps in Gujarat.
West Bengal State Legal Services Authority: no SIR or tribunal help desk found.
Association for Democratic Reforms: litigant, but no help service to electors found.

left_out.name: Inner Wheel Club of Bangalore South Parade
left_out.why: The page records one member volunteering one day (benefit count 1); not an organisational service.

left_out.name: Citizen Matters RWA volunteers, South Bengaluru
left_out.why: Informal neighbourhood volunteers named as individuals; no organisation.

left_out.name: Christian Minority Commission chairman (Telangana)
left_out.why: Appears to be a government body; role unclear.
